title: Searching for a Lost Plane

source.pdf_page_offset_note: Physical PDF pages and printed Page n of 34 labels agree one-to-one across pages 1-34.

notes: All 34 physical pages were read sequentially through the title, contents, every substantive section, Tables 1-9, press paper, and References 1-19.

Eight one-at-a-time byte-bounded JPEG proxies totaling 1,854,278 bytes covered pages 1-34 and focused the piecewise collision rule, branch weights, and normalized Bayes formula; no original full-page PNG entered model context.
Seven displayed equations or equation families, Figures 1-14, and Tables 1-9 have source-ordered retention and dispositions.

No clipping, overlap, missing page, blank page, black box, or formula-rendering failure was found; source formula, parameter, cross-reference, optimization, validation, and scope defects remain last-pass warnings.
The official problem statement is not frozen with this paper, so task reconstruction is bounded to the paper's explicit objectives and outputs.

section_map.summary: Input: A lost aircraft in open water, sparse incident evidence, heterogeneous search aircraft, and a two-stage maritime search problem. Analytical job: Name drifter-count estimation, current-driven simulation, surface and underwater Bayesian updates, branch-and-bound allocation, AF447/MH370 applications, and sensitivity. Output: A conditional promise that the system can prioritize search regions and resources for a declared incident scenario. Handoff: The contents and introduction unpack the model stages, case evidence, evaluation, public explanation, and source record.

Input: The summary's collision, search, allocation, application, and evaluation promise. Analytical job: Order base analysis; five assumption groups; notation; collision, simulation, Bayesian, surface, underwater, and allocation models; two applications; six sensitivity subsections; evaluation; press paper; references. Output: A complete source-heading map for the 34-page argument. Handoff: The introduction supplies the delayed-recovery context and seven explicit tasks.

Input: The unresolved MH370 search, AF447's nearly two-year underwater recovery, sparse data, and poorly charted ocean geography. Analytical job: Require drifter count, drift simulation, sequential Bayesian search, aircraft allocation, AF447 retrospective use, MH370 prediction, and strengths/weaknesses analysis. Output: Seven observable deliverables for an open-water missing-aircraft search system. Handoff: Base analysis identifies which target and platform attributes enter those deliverables.

section_map.section: 3 Base Analysis / 3.1 Type of Plane Crashed / 3.2 Type of Search Plane
section_map.summary: Input: Candidate crashed-aircraft types and helicopter/fixed-wing search platforms with different physical and sensing properties. Analytical job: Connect aircraft size, passenger capacity, and material to drifter count; connect search speed, range, and sensors to cell coverage and detection. Output: Two typed parameter families for the collision and allocation layers. Handoff: The assumptions state which real differences are retained, collapsed, or omitted.

Input: The target and platform heterogeneity identified in the base analysis. Analytical job: Fix full load, two disintegration regimes, equal fragments, simplified impulse, common initial target state, current-plus-random surface motion, static seabed parts, stationary targets during search, no false positives, aircraft-only assets, weather-invariant capability, and area limits replacing range. Output: A component-indexed assumption contract. Handoff: The notation table defines the quantities consumed under this contract.

Input: Collision, drift, search-state, and platform-detection concepts from Sections 3-4. Analytical job: Define N0, N, V, m, alpha, beta, v, theta, I, S_i,j, D, F(D), P_C, P_D, P_W, P_AkD, and P_AkW. Output: A notation interface for the physical and Bayesian models. Handoff: The collision model first uses N0, N, V, alpha, beta, v, theta, and I.

section_map.section: 6.1 Collision Model / 6.1.1 Air Disintegration / 6.1.2 Water Disintegration
section_map.summary: Input: Aircraft volume, total mass, impact velocity and angle, disintegration regime, and unobserved calibration constants. Analytical job: Set N0=alpha V; use N=beta N0; derive I=mv sin(theta); map impulse through a zero-linear-saturation beta function with I0 and gamma. Output: An actual drifter-count N for later surface-target reasoning. Handoff: The simulation module places those targets at the impact point and evolves synthetic trajectories.

Input: An impact location, generated drifters, current data, and an unspecified computer-random motion process. Analytical job: Initialize targets together, apply current-based motion plus random motion, and generate debris distributions and trajectories. Output: A simulated target-location history intended for model measurement and correction. Handoff: The Bayesian overview defines how actual search reports, rather than hidden simulator state, update location beliefs.

section_map.section: 6.3 Overview on Search Model / 6.3.1 Review on Bayesian Filtering Algorithm / 6.3.2 Steps of Search Plan
section_map.summary: Input: Unknown target cell S_i,j, accessible information, binary search reports B, and separate surface/underwater phases. Analytical job: Define a location prior, observation likelihood, posterior, recursive update, and the surface-to-underwater handoff shown in Figure 2. Output: A two-phase Bayesian state-estimation and control loop. Handoff: Section 6.4 constructs the surface prior from flight dynamics and reverse drift.

section_map.section: 6.4 Water Surface Search Model / 6.4.1 Surface Search Prior PDF / 6.4.2 Surface Search Posterior PDF
section_map.summary: Input: Last-known-position reachability, a nine-accident distance curve, reverse-drift evidence from spotted targets, OSCAR currents, search cells, and binary reports. Analytical job: Mix equal-probability LKP reachability with F(D)=1-22/(D^2+22) at 50/50; reverse-interpolate currents with a 0.25 speed factor; mix flight and drift priors at 70/30; apply normalized Bayes updating over the current search area. Output: A surface-search prior and posterior PDF over cells. Handoff: The underwater model reuses the surface posterior with the flight-dynamics prior.

Input: The surface posterior, flight-dynamics prior, underwater platform likelihood, and phase-specific detection reports. Analytical job: Mix 30% surface posterior with 70% flight prior; suspend surface search; replace drifter states and likelihoods with wreckage states and likelihoods in Bayes' rule; recurse after misses. Output: Phase-indexed underwater priors and posteriors until detection or intentional suspension. Handoff: The allocation model assigns available aircraft to high-probability cells in either phase.

section_map.section: 7 Allocation Model / 7.1 Review on Algorithms / 7.2 Allocation of Search Planes
section_map.summary: Input: An updated cell PDF and search aircraft with heterogeneous area limits and detection rates. Analytical job: Sort cells and aircraft in descending order, match stronger aircraft to larger cell probabilities, and state cumulative detection probability as the branch-and-bound maximization objective. Output: A ranked aircraft-to-cell allocation plan. Handoff: The application section uses the probability pipeline on AF447 and MH370, though it does not expose a complete allocation trace.

section_map.section: 8 Applying of Model / 8.1 Application on AF447 / 8.2 Prediction on MH370
section_map.summary: Input: AF447 recovery data and initial-search drifter distribution; MH370 satellite/radar path analyses, accessible probability regions, and assumed nondetections. Analytical job: For AF447, mix flight prior and initial surface evidence and compare the highest-probability region with the known wreckage point; for MH370, adopt an external path distribution and propagate no-detection updates through the search phases. Output: An AF447 underwater-prior map and four MH370 phase PDFs. Handoff: Sensitivity analysis varies selected target, resource, and mixture inputs around the paper's unspecified baseline case.

Input: A cumulative wreckage-detection metric, selected drifter counts, fleet sizes, nine platform profiles, and three pairs of mixture weights. Analytical job: Evaluate N in {50,100,200}; fleet count in {2,3,4}; selected two-plane combinations; and 30/70, 50/50, 70/30 weight pairs for three prior mixtures. Output: Six small deterministic sensitivity tables and directional interpretations. Handoff: Strengths and weaknesses convert these local responses and applications into broader claims and admitted limits.

Input: The AF447 region comparison, qualitative computation claims, local weight sweeps, and the assumption and parameter record. Analytical job: Claim accuracy, efficiency, application value, and robustness; admit scaling limits, unrealistic target simplifications, difficult detection parameters, and unrealistic fleet counts. Output: A paired capability-and-risk record requiring claim downgrades where evidence is absent. Handoff: The press paper translates the intended system for a public audience.

Input: Public concern about MH370, ocean uncertainty, the surface/underwater Bayesian plan, aircraft allocation, and AF447 comparison. Analytical job: Explain current and leeway evidence, rapid response, surface target observations, underwater posterior updates, stronger-plane-to-higher-probability allocation, and continued search. Output: A public narrative of evidence, action, feedback, redeployment, and termination. Handoff: References identify the external reports, data, search theory, and algorithm sources behind the narrative.

Input: Claims about AF447, MH370, ocean currents, Bayesian search, quicksort, branch-and-bound, and flight-path regions. Analytical job: Map nineteen citations to incident reports, OSCAR data, drift studies, Bayesian search theory, algorithms, and MH370 search geometry. Output: A provenance map with books and reports alongside incomplete web and data citations. Handoff: The paper terminates without frozen datasets, source code, simulation logs, or optimization traces.

assumptions.summary: The plane is fully loaded; accidents are divided into air and water disintegration; all broken pieces share one size.
Water impact is treated as an ideal collision with negligible horizontal impulse.
All drifters begin at the impact point and bodies and aircraft debris receive the same modeled movement effects.
Surface drift is generated only from current data plus unspecified computer random motion.
Underwater parts remain static after reaching the seafloor.
Surface drifters share movement and detection probability and remain stationary during each search phase.
No signal is available from the crashed aircraft and search vehicles are restricted to aircraft.
Aircraft capability is reduced to area limit and detection rate and is invariant to weather.
Underwater sensing reaches beyond seafloor depth.
Sensors have no false positives but may miss a present target.
Voyage constraints are replaced by search-area limits.
At most one drifter occupies a cell for the surface Bayes update.
MH370 surface and underwater phases are treated as nondetections for conditional propagation.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: AF447 and MH370 histories establish delayed-recovery stakes but are contextual cases, not a calibration sample.
Aircraft size, passenger load, material, crash state, and debris type motivate the target-count interface.
Table 1 compares three real search platforms by speed, voyage, and sensors, while later capability types are synthetic.
Table 2 defines N0, N, V, m, alpha, beta, v, theta, I, cell probabilities, and surface/underwater detection terms.
The system module uses an OSCAR current date, interpolation, a one-quarter current-speed coefficient, and random motion without freezing inputs.
Nine cited loss-of-control accidents provide the distance curve combined with LKP reachability.
Reverse drift depends on marine geography, surface currents, winds, spotted drifters, and backward trajectory construction.
Surface search reports B and aircraft-cell detection probability feed the normalized posterior.
Aircraft ranking uses area limit and surface/underwater detection probabilities as its capability interface.
AF447 wreckage location, date, depth, and initial-search information are drawn from the BEA report.
MH370 arc maps and constrained autopilot/data-error regions are imported from cited analyses.
Sensitivity inputs include N, fleet count, nine synthetic capability types, and three sets of prior-mixture weights.

writing_logic.summary: abstract: Preview the positive physical-to-probabilistic-to-allocation workflow before naming sensitivity and limitations. The contents and introduction unpack the model stages, case evidence, evaluation, public explanation, and source record.

title: Expose all source sections and keep surface search, underwater recursion, allocation, cases, sensitivity, public communication, and references distinct. The introduction supplies the delayed-recovery context and seven explicit tasks.

introduction: Turn public incidents into a bounded modeling and decision agenda rather than a general call for rescue technology. Base analysis identifies which target and platform attributes enter those deliverables.

problem-analysis: Separate target-generation factors from search-capability factors before they are combined in one plan. The assumptions state which real differences are retained, collapsed, or omitted.
assumptions: Expose the operating regime of every downstream physical, simulation, probabilistic, and allocation result. The notation table defines the quantities consumed under this contract.

notation: Keep maximum and actual target counts, crash mechanics, spatial probabilities, and surface/underwater likelihoods distinguishable. The collision model first uses N0, N, V, alpha, beta, v, theta, and I.

model-establishment: Separate maximum searchable material from the fraction released by a particular collision. The simulation module places those targets at the impact point and evolves synthetic trajectories.

data-preprocessing: Introduce a synthetic environment for comparing search outputs with hidden target trajectories. The Bayesian overview defines how actual search reports, rather than hidden simulator state, update location beliefs.

problem-restatement: Give the reader a prediction-update contract and phase flow before any incident-specific prior is mixed. Section 6.4 constructs the surface prior from flight dynamics and reverse drift.

model-improvement: Keep each evidence source and weight visible while converting them into an updateable surface-search distribution. The underwater model reuses the surface posterior with the flight-dynamics prior.

robustness-verification: Turn the surface result into a recursive underwater plan without treating one failed phase as elimination. The allocation model assigns available aircraft to high-probability cells in either phase.

algorithm: Connect spatial priority to resource selection through a named, inspectable optimization objective. The application section uses the probability pipeline on AF447 and MH370, though it does not expose a complete allocation trace.

results: Demonstrate two distinct uses: retrospective region comparison and conditional prospective search distribution. Sensitivity analysis varies selected target, resource, and mixture inputs around the paper's unspecified baseline case.

sensitivity-robustness: Show local output response to named physical, resource, platform, and weight choices. Strengths and weaknesses convert these local responses and applications into broader claims and admitted limits.
strengths-limitations: Summarize claimed utility while exposing the evidence and implementation boundaries that control transfer. The press paper translates the intended system for a public audience.

memo: Translate mathematical states and updates into a chronological search commitment without equations. References identify the external reports, data, search theory, and algorithm sources behind the narrative.

references: Expose the external basis and the archival limits of contextual, data, model, and algorithm claims. The paper terminates without frozen datasets, source code, simulation logs, or optimization traces.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The summary previews collision, staged Bayesian search, allocation, two cases, sensitivity, and limitations as one operational chain; award status does not prove which move caused judging success.
The flowchart makes mixture weights and surface/underwater handoffs scannable before the detailed formulas.
The AF447 overlay provides an immediate real-case comparison, although its validation strength is limited to qualitative inclusion.
The press paper closes the technical-to-public loop after model, case, sensitivity, and limitation sections.

weaknesses.summary: N0=alpha V is structurally clear, but alpha is neither identified from aircraft/debris data nor given a unit-consistent value; it must remain an uncalibrated parameter.
The printed velocity components are v_x=cos(theta) and v_y=sin(theta), omitting multiplication by v and conflicting dimensionally with the later I=mv sin(theta) expression.
The prose calls m total weight while the impulse equation treats m as mass; units must be reconciled before numerical use.
The piecewise beta rule is explicit, but I0 and gamma have no data source, fitted values, units audit, or uncertainty, so it cannot yield a reproduced drifter count.

The system module combines current data and computer random motion without specifying distributions, time step, interpolation details, seeds, execution environment, or archived trajectories; its output is synthetic rather than an exact answer.
Equation (6) is retained as F(D)=1-2^2/(D^2+2^2) with medium transcription confidence, but the nine-accident sample, distance units, fitting criterion, residuals, and uncertainty are absent.
The 50/50 mixture of LKP reachability and accident-distance distributions is a cited heuristic choice, not a calibrated mixing estimate.

The reverse-drift model uses a 0.25 speed coefficient and linear current interpolation without a reproducible OSCAR snapshot, leeway model, interpolation equation, boundary treatment, or validation against tracked debris.
The 70/30 surface-prior mixture is justified qualitatively by current uncertainty but is not inferred from observations or stress-tested jointly with the drift model.
Equation (7) is a normalized Bayes form, but P(B|S_i,j), report semantics, detection rates, cell evidence, and numerical arrays are not parameterized, preventing posterior reproduction.
The surface update assumes at most one drifter per cell and identical drifter movement/detection despite a shared initial point and heterogeneous debris, with no grid-resolution check.

The underwater prior's 30/70 weights, wreckage likelihood PAkW, phase evidence, and stopping/suspension policy are not calibrated; recursion alone does not establish convergence or localization reliability.

The branch-and-bound claim lacks formal decision variables, constraints, bounds, branching rules, search trace, and optimality certificate; parallel rankings and a diagram do not reproduce the stated maximization.
AF447 validation consists only of the reported location lying inside a displayed suggestive area; region area, nominal coverage, baseline comparison, temporal holdout, and scoring rule are absent.

The MH370 result imports a cited arc distribution and assumes no detection in both search stages; without frozen data, likelihoods, or outcome validation it is a conditional scenario, not a verified wreckage prediction.
The nine synthetic aircraft types are not mapped to the real platforms in Table 1, and Table 6 repeats the 7+9 row; the capability experiment is therefore illustrative rather than fleet-calibrated.

Tables 3-9 vary one factor across only three or selected nominal cases with no joint perturbation, uncertainty interval, normalization audit, or external test; narrow local changes do not establish robustness, credibility, flexibility, or universality.

Application prose says the process follows Figure 1 although the probability workflow is Figure 2, and invokes drifter data from Table 3 before Table 3 appears as a later sensitivity table; cross-reference provenance is broken.

The strengths and press sections overstate accuracy, efficiency, robustness, reliability, and broad applicability relative to the paper's uncalibrated parameters, synthetic module, local sensitivity, and limited case checks.

independent_extensions.summary: Estimate alpha, debris size classes, buoyancy, passenger survival targets, and uncertainty from aircraft and crash data.
Replace the printed component equations with a unit-checked collision model and calibrate I0 and gamma from impact tests or simulations.
Archive current fields, leeway coefficients, interpolation, stochastic distributions, seeds, time step, and trajectory outputs.
Define sensor-specific true/false detection likelihoods, cell occupancy, grid resolution, and normalized sequential evidence updates.
Formulate a reproducible mixed-integer allocation with coverage, time, endurance, coordination, revisit, and uncertainty constraints.
Evaluate case regions with proper scores, nominal coverage, area, baselines, temporal holdouts, and multiple incidents.
Run global and joint sensitivity with calibrated parameter ranges, uncertainty propagation, and decision-stability metrics.
Publish machine-readable inputs, equations, plots, optimizer traces, software versions, execution logs, and regression tests.
